info.title: Neat Insight API
info.description:
Neat Insight provides an HTTP control plane for importing media, discovering viewer URLs, inspecting runtime health, and browsing the active workspace. The same API drives the Insight web application and can be used from scripts, test automation, or development tools.

## Before you begin

- The default local endpoint is `https://127.0.0.1:9900`. Development installations normally use a locally generated certificate, so diagnostic clients may need to trust mkcert or use `curl -k`.
- Call `GET /api/health` before a workflow to confirm that the backend is ready.
- Media and workspace paths are always relative to their managed root. Absolute paths and traversal outside those roots are rejected.
- vf viewer channel indexes are **zero-based**.
- Operations that import media may return a streaming `text/plain` progress response. Read through the final line before deciding whether the operation succeeded.

## Typical workflows

1. **Import media:** validate a YouTube URL, then import a clip of it into the media library.
2. **Open a viewer:** request `/api/viewer-url` so the URL reflects the current host and configured SDK channel capacity.
3. **Troubleshoot delivery:** check ingest statistics first; if RTP reaches vf but the browser still fails, continue with egress statistics.
4. **Inspect artifacts:** browse the workspace tree, search paths, and preview files or members inside MPK archives.

## Security

The API has no application-level authentication. Expose it only on trusted development networks and place an authenticated gateway in front of it if broader access is required.

tags.name: API documentation
tags.description: Open the embedded Swagger UI or download the authoritative OpenAPI 3.1 document for generators, validators, and external documentation systems.

tags.name: Service and system
tags.description: Confirm readiness and discover the environment in which Insight is running. These endpoints expose logs, optional tool availability, Neat component status, platform build metadata, and the LAN address inferred for browser-facing links.

tags.name: Diagnostics
tags.description: Observe Insight, vf ingest, and WebRTC delivery. Start with the compact views for active channels, then add `all=1&verbose=1` when diagnosing inactive ports, packet loss, malformed RTP, missing keyframes, RTCP feedback, or browser decode problems.

tags.name: Media imports
tags.description: Populate the media library with YouTube clips: validate a URL, then download and transcode a clip of it. The import streams human-readable progress.

tags.name: Viewer
tags.description: Generate the URL of the viewer page, reachable from the current browser and bounded to the configured channel capacity, and relay the viewer's WebRTC offers to vf. Viewer channel indexes are zero-based even though media-source slots are one-based.

tags.name: Workspace
tags.description: Explore files produced by Neat workflows without exposing arbitrary host paths. APIs support folders, bounded search, text preview, raw images, and virtual paths into MPK tar archives using `archive::member` syntax.

tags.name: DevKit shell
tags.description: Discover or start the optional hosted shell bridge for a configured remote DevKit. These operations report actionable availability and connection metadata rather than configuring the DevKit itself.

tags.name: GenAI Studio
tags.description: Reach the GenAI Studio backend running on a board (`run.sh`, port 5000 by default) through Insight, so the browser never calls the board directly. Configure the board address once, then call the Studio's own API under `/api/genai/`.

tags.name: Board
tags.description: Select the one board that board-facing features use. Insight runs commands locally when it is installed on the board, and otherwise over SSH to the SDK-paired DevKit or a manually entered address. Authentication uses the SSH keys of the account running Insight; no password is accepted or stored. Failures return `code` and `hint` fields that name the recovery step.

tags.name: Peripherals
tags.description: List the MIPI and USB cameras and ALSA microphones SiMa Sentinel reports on the selected board, preview a camera, and test a microphone. Sentinel discovers the devices and Insight reads its catalog. Discovery never captures frames or audio, opens a sound device, changes sensor controls, or publishes streams; only a camera preview or a microphone test, started explicitly, captures, and only while it runs. Each camera mode is Available or Unsupported, decided from Sentinel's report: its sensor is in the board's camera overlays, the ISP outputs its size, and its format is NV12 (a fixed fact about Neat's `CameraInput`, not queried from the board). Core has no audio input node, so microphones carry no verdict.

tags.name: Sentinel
tags.description: Read SiMa Sentinel telemetry from the selected board and control its traces. Sentinel serves its API on a unix socket that is never exposed over the network, so Insight reaches it from the board itself: in process when Insight runs on the board, and otherwise by running a small client there over SSH. Metric values are `null` when the board cannot measure them, never zero.

get.description: Returns the Swagger UI bundled with Insight. Use it for quick exploration against the current installation; use `/api/openapi.json` when a tool needs the machine-readable contract.

200.description: Swagger UI HTML page.

get.description: Returns the exact OpenAPI 3.1 document used by the embedded Swagger UI and the generated core documentation. The document is suitable for linting, client generation, contract tests, and documentation builds.

200.description: OpenAPI 3.1 document for the current Insight API.

get.description: A lightweight readiness probe that also reports the startup-scoped browser network configuration applied to vf and MediaMTX. Call this first from automation; a `200` response confirms that the Flask backend can accept subsequent API requests. A present but invalid `browser-ice-address` configuration prevents Insight from starting. A full HTTP(S) `launch-url` is reduced to its origin; an invalid launch URL preserves legacy request-host/port-map URL generation.

200.description: The backend is ready.

get.description: Reads a bounded tail of a whitelisted system log without exposing arbitrary filesystem paths. Use `EV74` for accelerator/runtime messages and `syslog` for broader platform diagnostics; the response is plain text rather than JSON.

200.description: Up to the latest 10,000 lines, bounded to 256 KiB.

get.description: Returns the latest point-in-time metrics assembled for the Insight dashboard, including CPU, memory, disk, temperature, MLA, remote-platform, and pipeline compatibility fields. `cpu_load` is the total CPU use in percent, also for a remote DevKit. The local reading covers the time since the previous reading by anyone (the metrics stream included), is taken without blocking, and is not refreshed more often than every 0.5 s. The payload is intentionally extensible, so clients should tolerate additional fields.

200.description: CPU, memory, disk, temperature, MLA, remote, and compatibility metrics.

get.description: Opens a long-lived server-sent events connection to the local metrics broker. Each SSE `data` field contains one JSON metrics event; clients should reconnect after network interruption and must not wait for the response body to terminate.

200.description: A long-lived server-sent event stream. Each data field contains a JSON metrics event.

get.description: Reports whether the helper executables used for probing, transcoding, and streaming are available on the backend `PATH`. This is a capability check only; a reported tool may still fail for an unsupported codec or input.

200.description: Availability of media helper executables on PATH.

get.summary: Get Neat system and component status
get.description: Runs the Neat system-information command and enriches its structured result with Insight URL and port data. Use it for a broad installation snapshot; use the diagnostics endpoints for live transport-level investigation.

200.description: Structured output from `neat --json`, enriched with Insight URL and port information. When the `neat` command is not installed the status is still 200 with the same shape: unknown fields are null or empty and a `missing` list names what could not be read (`["neat"]`). `missing` is absent when `neat` answered.

post.description: Inspects a YouTube URL without downloading the media and returns the title, duration, thumbnail, and supported Insight transcode targets. Call this before starting an import so a UI or script can show the user the actual clip metadata and reject unsupported inputs early.

200.description: Video title, duration, thumbnail, and supported import targets.

post.summary: Import and transcode a YouTube clip
post.description: Downloads the selected clip segment and transcodes it to an Insight-compatible MP4 rendition. The response is a streaming progress log; imports can take significant time and clients should keep the connection open through the final status line. Clip duration is capped at five minutes to bound resource use.

get.description: Identifies whether Insight is running directly on a SiMa DevKit and whether a remote DevKit was configured through the environment. Frontends use these flags to select appropriate workflows and messaging; this endpoint does not modify deployment configuration.

200.description: DevKit and remote-DevKit mode flags.

get.summary: Get DevKit shell availability and launch metadata
get.description: Returns whether the optional hosted shell bridge is configured and running, along with its port, target metadata, and a prefilled launch URL when available. Use this endpoint to decide whether to show, start, or open the shell experience without guessing deployment details.

200.description: Configuration, service status, port, and prefilled launch URL.

post.summary: Start the hosted DevKit shell bridge
post.description: Starts the optional backend service that hosts an interactive shell connection to the configured remote DevKit, then returns updated launch metadata. The DevKit connection must already be configured through the deployment environment; this operation does not accept or persist credentials.

200.description: Running service status and launch metadata.

get.summary: Get the GenAI Studio board settings
get.description: Returns the board address Insight relays GenAI calls to, whether it was configured or derived (`127.0.0.1` on a board, otherwise the paired DevKit's `DEVKIT_SYNC_DEVKIT_IP`).

200.description: Board address in use and stored settings.

500.description: Insight's `cfg.json` exists but could not be read (`cfg-unreadable`); nothing is relayed rather than falling back to another board.

post.summary: Set the GenAI Studio board settings
post.description: Sets or clears the board address. An empty string clears it; an omitted field is unchanged. The address must be `http(s)://host[:port]` with no path. Settings persist in Insight's `cfg.json`.

200.description: Settings after the update.

500.description: Insight's `cfg.json` could not be read (`cfg-unreadable`; nothing is changed) or written (`cfg-unwritable`).

parameters.name: subpath
parameters.description: A GenAI Studio API path: `health`, `voices`, or one under `v1/`, `audio/`, `models/`, `benchmark/`, `tts/`, `piperplus/`, `supertonic/`, `voices/`, `rag/`, `board-camera/`. `shutdown` and every other path are refused.

get.summary: Relay a GET to the board's GenAI Studio backend
get.description: Forwards the request, with its query string, to the configured board and streams the response back unchanged: status, body, content type and the Studio's `X-*` headers. Server-sent event streams such as `models/logs/stream` pass through unbuffered, and binary answers such as the JPEG from `board-camera/snapshot?device=/dev/videoN` byte for byte. The board's self-signed certificate is accepted for the configured address only.

200.description: The board's response, passed through.

502.description: The board could not be reached.

500.description: Insight's `cfg.json` exists but could not be read (`cfg-unreadable`); nothing is relayed rather than falling back to another board.

503.description: No board address is configured or derivable (`not-configured`), or the saved address is not valid (`invalid-address`).

post.summary: Relay a POST to the board's GenAI Studio backend
post.description: Forwards the request body as sent (JSON or multipart audio uploads) to the configured board and streams the response back, so streamed chat replies arrive token by token.

200.description: The board's response, passed through.

502.description: The board could not be reached.

500.description: Insight's `cfg.json` exists but could not be read (`cfg-unreadable`); nothing is relayed rather than falling back to another board.

503.description: No board address is configured or derivable (`not-configured`), or the saved address is not valid (`invalid-address`).

get.description: Returns the board target, where it came from (`manual`, `on-board`, or `sdk-env`), the available defaults, and the last connection status. This call never connects to the board; use `POST /api/board/test` for a live check. `generation` changes whenever the target changes, so clients can discard data collected from a previous board.

200.description: Selected board and last known status.

post.summary: Select a board or restore the default
post.description: Saves `{host, port, user}` as the manually selected board, or clears the saved selection when the body is `{"reset": true}` so the on-board or SDK default applies again. The selection holds no credentials.

200.description: Updated board state.

post.description: Connects to the selected board and reads its host name, machine type, and build version. A changed SSH host key returns `409` with `host_key_changed`, both fingerprints, and a hint; trust the new key with `POST /api/board/trust-host-key` once you have confirmed the board was reflashed.

200.description: Board state with `status.state` set to `connected`.

post.summary: Trust a reflashed board's new host key
post.description: Replaces Insight's stored SSH host key for the selected board with the key it presented during the last failed connection. The fingerprint must match `presented_fingerprint` from that `host_key_changed` error.

200.description: Updated board state.

get.description: Returns the snapshot from the last `POST /api/peripherals/refresh` of the selected board. Before the first scan, or after the selected board changes, `scanned_at` is `null` and `items` is empty. This call never connects to the board.

200.description: Last peripheral snapshot, or an empty one.

post.summary: Scan the selected board for cameras and microphones
post.description: Asks SiMa Sentinel on the board (`/run/simaai-sentinel/api.sock`, `POST /v1/peripherals/refresh`) to rescan; Sentinel answers with the catalog of a scan that started after the request (it returns `504` after 10 s and `429` when 8 refreshes already wait). Over SSH the socket is reached with a stdlib `python3` helper. Each mode's `support` comes from Sentinel's catalog alone (see `SupportTier`). Microphones are Sentinel's ALSA capture devices, read from `/proc/asound` and sysfs without opening a sound device; their `availability` is Sentinel's own, passed through. A camera whose provider failed keeps Sentinel's last good modes (`modes_source: previous-scan`). `changes` lists devices added or removed since the previous refresh. Concurrent refreshes of one board share a single scan. Sentinel errors (not installed, not running, discovery disabled, too old, malformed answer) return `503` or `502` with an install or update hint.

200.description: New peripheral snapshot.

get.description: Returns the preview session for the selected board, or `null`. Never contacts the board. A session belongs to one board generation; selecting another board invalidates it.

200.description: The current preview session, or null.

post.description: Starts an explicit, temporary capture: over the board connection Insight runs a GStreamer pipeline (`gst-launch-1.0`; `libcamerasrc` for a MIPI camera, `v4l2src` on the camera's `/dev/v4l/by-id` path for a USB camera) that scales the mode to at most 640 pixels wide at up to 15 fps and writes JPEG frames to its stdout. Insight answers once the first frame arrived (within 10 s, or two frame periods for a mode slower than 0.2 fps, at most 60 s) and relays the frames at `stream_url`. Discovery never starts capture; only this call does. The mode defaults to the camera's `default_selection` and must be one the last scan listed: for a MIPI camera an `available` or `unverified` mode in NV12, for a USB camera any listed mode in MJPG or a raw format (YUYV, UYVY, YVYU, NV12, NV21, YU12, YV12, GREY, RGB3, BGR3). The rate is the scan's exact fraction (`framerate_num`/`framerate_den`). A camera listed from SiMa Sentinel's last successful scan, because its provider failed during the refresh (`modes_source: previous-scan`), is refused with 503 `peripheral_unavailable`: its device may have changed since. Insight refuses a camera the scan or a check just before the start finds in use, or one the pipeline cannot acquire (409 `camera_in_use`); a board without `gst-launch-1.0`, or without a GStreamer element the pipeline needs (named in `tool`), returns 502 `tool_missing` with the packages to install; a pipeline that fails or sends no frame returns 502 `command_failed` with its output in `detail`. While a preview runs the camera cannot be opened by an application. Capture stops on `stop`, when its stream response ends, when nobody opens the stream within 15 s, when a refresh starts, or when the selected board changes.

200.description: The preview session.

get.description: Relays the preview's JPEG frames as a long-lived `multipart/x-mixed-replace; boundary=frame` response, one `image/jpeg` part with a `Content-Length` per frame, for an `` element. Insight checks the board's framing and refuses a frame over 4 MiB. One viewer per session: a second request returns 409 `preview_active`. When the response ends (the viewer disconnects, or the board sends nothing for 10 s, or for two frame periods for a mode slower than 0.2 fps, at most 60 s) the preview stops on the board. An unknown or superseded session id returns 404.

200.description: Long-lived multipart JPEG stream.

post.description: Closes the stream and stops the pipeline on the board by its process id (TERM, then KILL after 2 s), which releases the camera. Returns the stopped session, or `null` when that session already ended, so a repeated stop succeeds; an older session id never stops a newer session. The stream is closed first, so a pipeline whose kill command fails still ends at its next write; the session is kept for a retry only when the stream's own cleanup has not already released it.

200.description: The stopped session, or null.

post.description: Starts recording from a scanned microphone on the board and returns `202` at once. It records until `POST .../test/stop` or for `seconds` (at most 30); poll `GET` for the live level and the result. Insight first re-reads SiMa Sentinel's catalog: when that microphone's capture target or identity changed since the scan (a replug, or a restarted Sentinel routing the id elsewhere), it returns `409 stale_snapshot` without recording; other catalog changes, such as a previewing camera's rate, do not count; it also refuses a microphone whose provider data is from an earlier scan (`409 stale_snapshot`), and one without a safe Sentinel selector (`502 peripheral_response`). Sentinel's availability is not used to refuse: Insight then checks the capture PCM on the board and returns `409 microphone_in_use`, naming the holding process where it can see it, only when a substream is open now. The board runs `arecord` on Sentinel's `plughw:CARD=<id>,DEV=<n>` selector, converted to 16-bit PCM at 48 kHz when the device offers it (else its nearest rate below, never above 48 kHz) and at most two channels. Only one test records at a time (`409 test_running`). Returns `409 stale_snapshot` when the selected board changed since the scan. A busy device, a board without `arecord`, or a failed recording ends the test with `state: failed` and the error.

get.description: The latest microphone test on the selected board: while it records, its elapsed time and the level of the audio just received, for a live meter; once finished, its level and `audio_url`, or its error. `null` before any test, and once a scan lists another device under the microphone's id (a replug in the same port). Never contacts the board.

200.description: The test, or null.

post.description: Ends the test named by `token` on the selected board at once; a token that is not the current test's (a late Stop for an earlier test) stops nothing and returns null. It ends the recording even when `arecord` has stopped producing audio; what was recorded becomes the result, read through `GET` as usual. A test stopped before 0.1 s was recorded ends with `stopped_early`. Returns the test, or null when there is none for the selected board. It never stops another application.

200.description: The test, or null.

get.description: The finished recording of the selected board as 16-bit PCM WAV. `404` once a newer test replaced it, another board was selected, or a scan lists another device under the microphone's id.

200.description: The recording.

get.summary: Get Sentinel availability on the selected board
get.description: Reports whether the `simaai-sentinel` daemon is installed, running and answering on its unix socket, together with its version and the board it belongs to. A daemon that is missing, stopped or unreadable is reported as `available: false` with `status.state` and `status.error`, not as an HTTP failure; only board-level failures (no board selected, unreachable, timeout) use an error status. The daemon state is cached briefly per board, so polling this endpoint does not run a command on the board for every call. Pass `refresh=1` for an explicit re-check that bypasses this cache.

parameters.name: refresh
parameters.description: Set to `1` to bypass the short-lived daemon-status cache.

200.description: Sentinel availability for the selected board.

post.summary: Install Sentinel on the selected board
post.description: Runs `sima-cli neat install sentinel` on the board itself (the installer has no `--ip`) with `SIMA_INSTALL_CONTEXT=1`, `SIMA_CLI_CHECK_FOR_UPDATE=0` and a temporary download directory, using passwordless sudo. An installed and healthy daemon is never reinstalled: the installer restarts the daemon and would end a trace in flight, so that case returns `409 already_installed`. Without passwordless sudo the response names the exact command to run on the board.

parameters.name: generation
parameters.description: The board `generation` of the Sentinel state that offered installation. Recommended: a request that outlives a board switch returns `409 stale_snapshot` instead of installing on the board selected now.

200.description: Sentinel installed; the new daemon state and the installer's output.

get.description: Joins Sentinel's metric definitions with its latest sample so every value carries its label, unit, group and thresholds, and ranks each value as `ok`, `warn`, `critical` or `unavailable`. A metric the board cannot measure has `value: null` and status `unavailable`; it is never reported as zero. Definitions are cached per board for a minute, while the sample is read on every call. Samples are also appended to a bounded per-board history: pass `history=<n>` to get the last `n` samples as aligned per-metric series. The history holds one run of polling: a sample more than a minute after the last one starts it again, since nothing polls this endpoint while the Stats page is closed, and so does a restart of the daemon, which every call checks. To poll incrementally, send the newest `history.timestamps` entry you hold as `after` and the `history.epoch` it came with as `epoch`: the answer then holds only the samples after it, with `history.full: false`, and you append them. A reset, gap, restart or reseed of the history (a new `epoch`), an `after` the history no longer holds, or more new samples than `history` asks for answer the whole window with `history.full: true`, which replaces what you hold. Cached samples, definitions and history are keyed by the board's generation and fingerprint, so selecting another board starts empty.

parameters.name: history
parameters.description: Number of recent samples to return as series; `0` (the default) returns none. A value above 240, the most the history holds, is treated as 240.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: The timestamp of the newest sample you hold, from `history.timestamps`. With the `epoch` of that history, the answer holds only the samples after it; without either, or if it is not in the history, the answer is the whole window.

parameters.name: epoch
parameters.description: The `history.epoch` of the history you hold. A different epoch means the history started again or gained older samples, so the answer is the whole window with `full: true`. Not a whole number returns `400 invalid_request`.

200.description: Current metric values for the selected board.

get.description: Returns Sentinel's active trace and its running summary in `sentinel`, or `trace: null` when nothing is being recorded.

200.description: The active trace, if any.

post.description: Starts recording a named trace around a workload. Only one trace can be active and names must be unique, so a second start returns `409 trace_conflict` with Sentinel's own message. The request is validated before it reaches the board: a missing or empty name, a name containing a comma, an over-long note, or tags that are not a list of non-empty strings return `400 invalid_request` without touching it.

parameters.name: generation
parameters.description: The board `generation` of the active-trace payload the form was shown with. Recommended: a request that outlives a board switch returns `409 stale_snapshot` instead of starting a trace on the board selected now.

200.description: The trace Sentinel started.

post.description: Stops the active trace and persists it as a run, returning Sentinel's answer in `sentinel`. Returns `409 trace_conflict` when no trace is active or, when `trace_id` is sent, when the active trace is another one, and `409 stale_snapshot` without touching the board when `generation` names a board that is no longer selected. Current Sentinel versions compare `trace_id` and stop under one run-store lock; older schema-1 daemons retain their compatible check-then-stop behavior.

parameters.name: generation
parameters.description: The board `generation` of the active-trace payload being stopped. Recommended: a request that outlives a board switch is refused instead of stopping a trace on another board.

parameters.name: trace_id
parameters.description: The `id` of the trace being stopped, from `/api/sentinel/traces`. Recommended: a current Sentinel atomically returns `409 trace_conflict` instead of stopping a trace that replaced it on the same board. Without it, whichever trace is active is stopped.

200.description: The run Sentinel saved.

get.description: Returns Sentinel's recording and completed run summaries in `sentinel.runs`, newest retention first. Runs are stored on the board and survive a daemon restart.

200.description: Run summaries held by the board.

get.description: Returns one run by unique name or stable id, with its metadata, metric definitions and raw samples, in `sentinel`. An unknown or ambiguous name returns `404 not_found` with Sentinel's message. A run whose answer exceeds the 12 MiB Insight reads from the daemon (about three hours of samples) returns `502 response_too_large` with the limit in `limit_bytes`, rather than a truncated body.

parameters.name: run_id
parameters.description: The run's unique name or stable id.

200.description: The saved run.

delete.description: Permanently deletes one completed run from the board and returns the deleted run's `id` and `name` in `deleted`, with Sentinel's run list afterwards in `sentinel`. Sentinel's API has no delete, so Insight resolves the name or id against the daemon's run list first and then runs `simaai-sentinel runs delete <id>` on the board with the id the daemon reported; the path value itself is never passed to the board. A run Sentinel does not list returns `404 not_found` without running anything. A run that is still recording returns `409 trace_conflict`; stop the trace first. When `generation` is sent and the selected board has changed since, `409 stale_snapshot` is returned and nothing is deleted. A CLI failure keeps its output in `detail`: `tool_missing` when `simaai-sentinel` is not on the board, `sentinel_denied` when the board user may not remove the file, and `sentinel_failed` otherwise, including when the run is still listed afterwards.

parameters.name: run_id
parameters.description: The run's unique name or stable id, as `GET /api/sentinel/runs` reports it.

parameters.name: generation
parameters.description: The board `generation` of the run list the run was chosen from. Recommended: a request that outlives a board switch is refused instead of deleting a run of the same name on another board.

200.description: The run was deleted. `deleted` names it; `sentinel.runs` is the run list after the delete.

get.description: Compares two or more runs on the same elapsed timeline and returns run metadata, per-run statistics and deltas against the first run, which is the baseline. `raw=1` adds timestamped samples and is much larger. Fewer than two runs, or more than eight, return `400 invalid_request` without touching the board; an unknown run returns `404 not_found`.

parameters.name: runs
parameters.description: Comma-separated run names or ids; the first is the baseline.

parameters.name: raw
parameters.description: Include timestamped samples in the comparison.

200.description: The comparison Sentinel computed.

get.summary: Get local or remote platform build information
get.description: Returns parsed SiMa release and platform metadata for the active environment. On a remote-DevKit installation the backend retrieves the target's build information; without a DevKit it falls back to host platform details. A `502` generally means the configured remote target could not be reached or read.

200.description: Parsed SiMa build metadata, or host platform details when no DevKit is configured.

get.description: Resolves the address that browser-facing links should use, preferring `CONTAINER_HOST_IP`, then an inferred LAN address, and finally `127.0.0.1`. This is intended for URL construction in container and bridge-network deployments, not as a complete network-interface inventory.

200.description: Configured or inferred LAN IP.

get.description: Reports the logical root used by all workspace endpoints and whether the conventional `/workspace` mount is active. Returned paths establish context for the browser but subsequent API requests must still use relative workspace paths.

200.description: Resolved workspace root and whether `/workspace` is active.

get.summary: List a workspace folder or MPK archive folder
get.description: Lists the immediate children of a workspace directory or a directory inside an MPK tar archive. Use an empty path for the root and `archive_mpk.tar.gz::member/path` for archive navigation. Results are sorted and classified so clients can build a lazy-loading file browser without extracting archives.

200.description: Folder path and sorted immediate children.

get.description: Performs a bounded, case-insensitive search across workspace filesystem names and relative paths. MPK archives are searchable as files, but members inside them are not indexed; browse an archive with the workspace tree endpoint instead. Results are ranked and capped at 200 entries. Supply `kind` to narrow broad queries to models, images, code, text, archives, executables, or binary files.

200.description: Up to 200 ranked matches.

get.description: Returns classification and filesystem metadata for one file, folder, archive, or MPK member without reading its content. Use this when a client needs size, modification time, or preview strategy before requesting the file-preview or raw-image endpoint.

200.description: File, folder, or MPK archive-member metadata.

get.description: Returns original image bytes for an ordinary image file in the workspace filesystem. MPK archive-member paths are not supported by this endpoint. This route is intended for browser `` sources and binary consumers; use the JSON file-preview endpoint for text and metadata. Non-image or inaccessible paths return an error rather than arbitrary file bytes.

200.description: Raw image bytes using the detected media type.

get.summary: Preview a workspace file or MPK archive member
get.description: Returns node metadata together with a bounded text preview when the selected content is text-like. The `previewAvailable` and `truncated` flags tell clients whether content was returned and whether only a prefix is shown. Binary files remain discoverable but are not serialized into the JSON response.

200.description: Node metadata and a bounded text preview when the content is text-like.

WorkspacePath.name: path
WorkspacePath.description: Relative workspace path. MPK members use `archive_mpk.tar.gz::member/path`.

RequiredWorkspacePath.name: path
RequiredWorkspacePath.description: Relative workspace path. MPK members use `archive_mpk.tar.gz::member/path`.

ProgressStream.description: Streaming progress messages. Inspect the final lines to determine whether the operation completed or failed.

Forbidden.description: The requested path escapes the allowed root.

NotFound.description: The requested resource was not found.

Conflict.description: The resource's current state does not permit the requested operation, for example a slot that is not running, is held by an external publisher, or was stopped, reassigned, reset or unassigned while its FPS rendition was being prepared (start it again).

BadGateway.description: A required backend command, vf, DevKit, or remote catalog service failed or returned an invalid response.

GatewayTimeout.description: A required backend command or media helper timed out.

BoardErrorResponse.description: The board or a command on it could not be used. `code` identifies the failure and `hint` names the recovery step.

Error.description: Standard JSON error envelope returned by most failed API operations.

error.description: Human-readable failure reason suitable for logs and user-facing diagnostics.

GenaiError.description: Error from the GenAI relay itself (not from the board), with a machine-readable reason.

example.error: GenAI Studio backend unreachable at https://192.168.2.3:5000: [Errno 61] Connection refused

GenaiSettings.description: Board address Insight relays GenAI calls to, and stored settings.

url.description: Address in use; empty when none is configured or derivable.

configuredUrl.description: Address set by the user, or null.

defaultUrl.description: Address used when none is configured, or null.

GenaiSettingsUpdate.description: Fields to change; an empty string clears a value.

url.description: `http(s)://host[:port]` of the board's GenAI Studio backend.

HostMetrics.description: Point-in-time readings of the machine Insight runs on, or of the remote DevKit when one is configured.

cpu_load.description: Total CPU use in percent. `""` for a remote DevKit that is not connected; null when the remote DevKit's `top` gave no reading.

memory.description: Memory use; empty when it could not be read (a remote DevKit that is not connected).

disk.description: Use of the volume holding Insight's data; empty (remote DevKit) or null when it could not be read.

temperature_celsius_avg.description: Average board temperature in degrees Celsius; null when the platform has no reading.

REMOTE.description: True when the readings come from a remote DevKit.

Health.description: Readiness result for the Insight Flask backend.

status.description: Fixed readiness state returned when the backend can serve requests.

service.description: Stable service identifier for automated probes.

time.description: Backend UTC time when the response was created.

network.description: Startup-scoped browser networking values applied by this Insight process.

browser_ice_address.description: Address advertised to browsers by vf and MediaMTX, or null when no override is active. The opt-in browser-ice-address file accepts IPv4; a legacy CONTAINER_HOST_IP fallback can also be IPv6.

browser_ice_address_source.description: Configuration source used for the effective browser ICE address.

public_origin.description: Trusted browser-facing HTTP origin used for viewer, WHIP, and MJPEG URLs, or null for request-host and port-map behavior.

YoutubeUrlRequest.description: YouTube video URL to inspect or import.

url.description: Public YouTube watch or share URL supported by the backend downloader.

YoutubeImportRequest.description: Selects the output rendition and optional bounded clip range for a YouTube import.

target.description: Insight-compatible resolution and frame-rate rendition to generate.

clip_duration.description: Number of seconds to import, capped at five minutes.

WorkspaceKind.description: Content classification used for workspace icons, filtering, and preview selection.

WorkspaceNode.description: Metadata for one workspace filesystem entry or virtual member inside an MPK archive.

name.description: Display name of the filesystem entry or archive member.

path.description: Relative workspace path accepted by other workspace endpoints; archive members use `archive::member` syntax.

type.description: Structural node type used to distinguish files from navigable folders. MPK archives have type `folder` and kind `archive`.

size.description: Content size in bytes when known.

archive.description: Containing MPK archive path for a virtual member; omitted for ordinary filesystem entries.

WorkspaceTree.description: One level of a lazily browsable workspace directory or MPK archive directory.

path.description: Relative folder or archive-member directory that was listed.

archive.description: Containing MPK archive when the listed directory is virtual.

children.description: Sorted immediate children; descendants are loaded with subsequent tree requests.

WorkspaceFilePreview.description: Workspace node metadata plus a bounded textual preview when the content type is safe to represent as text.

content.description: Decoded text prefix, or an empty string when no text preview is available.

truncated.description: Whether content continues beyond the returned bounded preview.

previewAvailable.description: Whether the selected node was classified as safely previewable text.

BoardError.description: Error envelope for board and peripheral operations.

generation.description: Sentinel endpoints only: the board `generation` that answered with the failure, present once the selected board is known, so a client can discard a failure from a board other than the one it asked.

hint.description: Concrete recovery step, such as the `ssh-copy-id` command to run.

command.description: `auth_failed` only: the command that authorizes an SSH key on the board.

tool.description: `tool_missing` only: the command that was not found on the board.

detail.description: The underlying error text, such as SiMa Sentinel's answer or the socket failure.

host.description: `host_key_changed` only: the known_hosts name of the board.

presented_fingerprint.description: `host_key_changed` only: SHA256 fingerprint the board presented.

example.error: SSH key authentication as sima on 192.168.2.2 failed.
example.hint: Insight signs in with the SSH keys of the 'root' account on this machine. Authorize one on the board, then retry: sudo -H ssh-copy-id -p 22 sima@192.168.2.2

source.description: `sdk-env` is the DevKit paired with `sima-cli sdk setup` (`DEVKIT_SYNC_DEVKIT_IP`, `_USER`, `_PORT`).

saved.description: Manually selected `{host, port, user}`, if any.

generation.description: Changes whenever the selected target changes.

board.description: Identity read from the board: `hostname`, `machine`, `build_version`, and a stable `fingerprint`.

reset.description: Clear the saved selection instead of saving one.

SupportTier.description: Whether a camera mode is usable, decided from SiMa Sentinel's catalog alone. A Sentinel that decides each mode itself (per-mode `available` and `reason`, sentinel#43) is followed, with its reason; on Platform 3.0 its modes are the sensor's sizes (`sensor_mode`), and IMX477 sizes wider than 4032 are `unsupported` because libcamera streams them at 4032 wide. For a Sentinel that does not decide, the same rule is applied here. `available`: Sentinel's `board` block lists the camera's sensor (the `configured_cameras` entry whose `camera_id` is the camera's id) among the sensors the board's camera overlays support (`supported_sensors`), the mode is an ISP output size (`isp_output`), and its format is NV12, which Neat's `CameraInput` outputs (a fixed fact, not queried from the board). `unsupported`: anything else, with `reason`: a USB camera, a sensor not in the board's camera overlays (also when no configured camera matches), a size the ISP cannot output, a format other than NV12, or a Sentinel that sends no `board` block (every mode). A camera or format is `available` when any of its modes is; otherwise its `reason` says why none is. `unverified` marks a Platform 3.0 sensor size Sentinel leaves without a verdict: libcamera may crop it from a larger mode, so it is selectable and previewable but never the default.

id.description: SiMa Sentinel's stable device id: `camera:<sensor entity name>` (MIPI) or `camera:v4l2:<hash of the USB port>` (USB).

connection.description: `mipi` or `usb`; a connection Insight does not group is passed through and not listed on the page.

device.description: Known identifiers from Sentinel: `camera_name`, `camera_name_source` (`media-graph`: the sensor entity Sentinel names the camera after), `media_device`, `bus_info`, and `csi` (CSI receiver) for MIPI; `video_node`, `by_id` (the /dev/v4l/by-id link), and `usb` identity (`vendor_id`, `product_id`, `manufacturer`, `serial`, `product`, `bus_path`, `speed_mbps`) for USB.

availability.description: SiMa Sentinel's own availability fact, passed through. Insight does not inspect the board's processes; a camera another program holds is reported when a preview tries to open it (`camera_in_use`).

exportable.description: Whether the format has an Available mode.

framerate_num.description: The exact rate as a fraction: value is framerate_num / framerate_den, rounded for display.

tier.description: The state of the mode this rate belongs to.

reason.description: Why the mode is Unverified or Unsupported; absent when it is Available.

default_selection.description: The first Available mode (`format`, `width`, `height`, `fps`); null when no mode is Available.

board.description: Label, source, host name, machine, build version, and fingerprint of the scanned board.

generation.description: Board generation the scan belongs to; compare with `GET /api/board`.

scan_id.description: Opaque identifier for this exact peripheral scan; null before the first scan.

changes.description: `added` and `removed` devices (`id`, `name`) compared with the previous refresh of the same board.

camera_setup.description: The board's camera setup from its device tree, as SiMa Sentinel reports it; null before the first scan or when Sentinel is too old to report it.

PreviewSession.description: An explicit, temporary capture whose JPEG frames Insight relays at `stream_url`.

id.description: Session id; every later call must present it.

stream_url.description: Same-origin path of the session's multipart JPEG stream.

viewer.description: Whether a page already shows this preview's stream, which has one viewer; only `GET /api/peripherals/preview` reports it.

camera_fps.description: The frame rate the camera runs at in this mode, or null while it is unknown. A USB camera's is the mode's rate, which the pipeline requests. A MIPI camera's is the most its sensor delivers in this mode: SiMa Sentinel's `max_fps` (computed at minimum blanking) from a rescan Insight requests after the first frame, when the sensor runs in this mode, so the page shows it as "up to"; it stays null when Sentinel does not report it. That rescan records no Insight scan and does not stop the preview.

PeripheralMicrophone.description: An ALSA capture device from SiMa Sentinel's catalog. There is no Neat configuration to export for it: Core has no audio input node.

id.description: Sentinel's device id, derived from the device's sysfs path and capture PCM, never from a card number. Stable across rescans and card renumbering.

record.description: A fingerprint of the scanned capture target and identity a microphone test binds to. It changes when a rescan lists another device under the same `id` (a replug in the same port); a test from before the change is gone.

name.description: USB product string, else Sentinel's name (the ALSA card name).

device.description: `card_index`, `card_id`, `card_name`, `card_driver`, `pcm_device`, `pcm_node` (`/dev/snd/pcmC<card>D<device>c`), `alsa_name` (`hw:CARD=<id>,DEV=<device>`), the card's `by_path` and `by_id` links when udev made them, `usb` identity and `part_of` (`id`, `name`) when the same USB device is also a camera item.

availability.description: SiMa Sentinel's own availability fact, passed through. Insight does not inspect the board's processes during a scan; a microphone another program has open is reported when its test starts (`409 microphone_in_use`).

capture.description: Each capture format, channel count, bit depth and rate set Sentinel reads from the USB-audio `/proc/asound/card<N>/stream<M>` file; `null` for other drivers, whose formats cannot be read without opening the device.

rates.description: Discrete sample rates in Hz; empty when `rate_range` is set.

rate_range.description: A continuous rate range in Hz.

id.description: A microphone `id` from the last scan.

seconds.description: The longest to record when nobody stops it.

device.description: The ALSA device recorded from: Sentinel's selector.

level_dbfs.description: While recording, the peak of the audio just received in dBFS; `null` for silence and once finished.

level.description: When ready: peak and RMS in dBFS (`null` for digital silence). `silent` is true when the typical level is below -60 dBFS, so a click on open does not count as sound.

audio_url.description: When ready: where to fetch the WAV.

SentinelBoard.description: The board the telemetry belongs to; `fingerprint` also keys Insight's per-board caches.

SentinelDaemon.description: What the board reports about the simaai-sentinel service.

installed.description: A simaai-sentinel unit or its socket exists on the board.

healthy.description: The service is active and its socket is present.

sima_cli.description: Path to sima-cli on the board, used to install Sentinel.

instance_id.description: systemd's invocation ID for the running daemon; it changes on every service restart. Null when the daemon is not running.

started_at.description: When the running daemon started, on Insight's clock: measured on the board as how long the service has been active, so a board clock that is wrong after a boot does not skew it. Null when the daemon is not running.

generation.description: Board selection generation; it bumps whenever the selected board changes.

available.description: Sentinel answered its API and speaks the schema Insight understands.

schema.description: The Sentinel API schema this Insight understands.

error.description: Why Sentinel cannot be used, with the step that fixes it.

health.description: Sentinel's `/v1/health` body: version, freshness, sample and metric counts, errors, and the active trace.

group.description: Sentinel's group, or `Other` for a value with no definition.

value.description: `null` when the board cannot measure it; never zero for a missing value.

sampled_at.description: Timestamp of the sample the values come from.

highlights.description: Keys the Stats page leads with: board power, CPU, Linux memory, MLA allocated memory, EV74 CMA memory, and the hottest temperature sensor the board reports.

order.description: Every metric key in Sentinel's own order, the order its ops view lists them in. A group's sensors are not always adjacent, so this is not the order of `groups`.

history.description: The samples of this board to add to the caller's window, aligned; empty unless `history` was requested. With `full: true` they are the last `history` samples and replace the window the caller holds, which is what a reset, gap, restart or reseed answers; with `full: false` they are the samples after `after`, to append. On the first read of a board, and again after a gap in polling of more than a minute, the history is seeded from Sentinel's own sample cache (its newest 240 samples, read once from `GET /v1/cache`), so it opens full rather than filling from polling.

full.description: `true` when the samples replace what the caller holds (always so without `after` and `epoch`, or with `history=0`); `false` when they only follow the sample at `after`.

epoch.description: Which history this is. It changes whenever the history starts again (another board, a daemon restart, a gap in polling, a clock step) or gains samples before the oldest, and never repeats; send it back as `epoch`.

SentinelPassthrough.description: Sentinel's own response body under `sentinel`, minus its `schema` marker, plus the board it came from. Nesting keeps a run's or comparison's fields from shadowing `board` and `generation`.

sentinel.description: The daemon's body, such as `{trace, summary}`, `{runs}`, `{run}` or a comparison.

name.description: Unique trace name of at most 80 UTF-8 bytes, without control characters or a comma (`/api/sentinel/compare` separates runs with commas); Sentinel rejects a name a run already uses.

model.description: The board model from its device tree.

overlays.description: The device-tree overlays the board loads that configure a camera sensor, in U-Boot's order: the entries of SiMa Sentinel's overlay list that some sensor in its `board.supported_sensors` names. Other overlays (PCIe, secure boot) are not listed.
